title: Scrumptious
projectNote: One shared app, five areas of ownership. Build the foundation together, then use small pull requests to keep main working.

architecture.title: One app with two role-specific experiences
architecture.rationale: Students enter and review decisions. Professors manage submissions, prepare files, import output, and release results. Shared components keep both sides consistent.
architecture.consequence: The role selector previews screens. It does not grant a real professor role. Verified student/professor permissions remain a production task.

architecture.title: Keep the FORTRAN engine external
architecture.rationale: The existing engine is the source of simulation outcomes. The app modernizes decisions, file preparation, and results without rewriting simulation formulas.
architecture.consequence: The professor downloads RFI files, runs FORTRAN manually, and imports the original FR.LST. There is no Run simulation button.

architecture.title: Preserve fixed-width files with tested templates
architecture.rationale: The supplied RFI examples include control fields whose meanings are not fully documented. Change only mapped fields and preserve reserved data, spacing, and original line endings.
architecture.consequence: Unedited decisions must reproduce all 30 supplied RFI examples byte for byte. Report flag names and business ranges need instructor confirmation.

architecture.title: Identify menu selections by line number
architecture.rationale: Firm 2 in Q2 offers STEAK twice, once as Sirloin and once as Burger. A key based only on menu item would discard one valid choice.
architecture.consequence: Use (TeamID, RoundNumber, LineNumber) for menu decisions and results. Separate imported outcomes from editable decisions.

architecture.title: Persist the prototype in a shared D1 workspace
architecture.rationale: Decisions, released results, design tokens, and planning notes need to survive reloads and appear across devices. D1 stores an atomic snapshot with an optimistic revision check.
architecture.consequence: The snapshot is the current runtime. The normalized SQL model is the proposed next step for the database area. Stale saves return a conflict instead of overwriting a newer edit.

architecture.title: Use desktop-first forms with four focused parts
architecture.rationale: Teams compare prices, portions, staffing, and budgets on laptops. Four parts group related decisions and show completion without crowding the home screen.
architecture.consequence: Menu, Staffing, Amenities & upkeep, and Management info share one draft. Users can jump directly to a part, then review the full strategy before submitting.
